title: SNC resolution of the good components of a semilinear Sylow quotient
statement: Let $e$ be a field, $\ell$ a prime different from $\operatorname{char}(e)$, and $K/e$ a finite field extension [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension]. Let $B$ be a nonempty normal proper finite-type $e$-scheme which is a finite disjoint union of integral schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-pc-integral-scheme]. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Let a finite group $G$ act on $K$ by $e$-automorphisms with $K^G/e$ purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], and on a smooth projective $K$-scheme $Y$ by $e$-scheme automorphisms, equivariantly for $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-kun-projective]. Suppose $h:Y\to B$ is an invariant projective surjection [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] sending every irreducible-component generic point to one of $B$ with finite residue extension [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-residue-field]. Suppose every subgroup quotient is a finite categorical geometric scheme quotient, with orbit geometric fibres and invariant structure sheaf, and $Y/G\to B$ is a finite universal homeomorphism over a dense open meeting every component [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. Let $C\subseteq B$ be closed, and suppose $D=(h^{-1}C)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a relative strict normal crossings divisor over $K$ [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor]. Then there are an $\ell$-Sylow subgroup $L\leq G$ (order a power of $\ell$, index prime to $\ell$), $F=K^L$ with $[F:e]$ prime to $\ell$ and $K/F$ finite separable, and an open and closed union $Q^\circ\subseteq Y/L$ of components, whose inverse image $Y^\circ\subseteq Y$ is open and closed. The restricted quotient $q:Y^\circ\to Q^\circ$ and induced projective surjection $d:Q^\circ\to B$ satisfy $h|_{Y^\circ}=d q$. Every generic point of $Q^\circ$ maps to a generic point of $B$, with finite residue degree prime to $\ell$. There are a smooth projective $F$-scheme $R$, a projective surjective $F$-morphism $v:R\to Q^\circ$, and a reduced relative strict normal crossings divisor $E\subseteq R$ such that $v$ induces a bijection on component generic points and equality of their residue fields, and $|E|=v^{-1}(q(|D\cap Y^\circ|))=(d v)^{-1}(C)$. The scheme $R$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]; $E$ is also a strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], and the components through any point have equations given by distinct members of a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Empty $C$ and nonfaithful actions are allowed. Degrees mean dimensions over the smaller field [def-pc-field-tower].

proof.text: Choose an $\ell$-Sylow subgroup $L\leq G$ by the Sylow existence and prime-index lemma. In particular $|L|=\ell^a$ for some $a\geq0$ and $[G:L]$ is prime to $\ell$.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, p.151, choice of L in diagram (2.c).

proof.text: Apply the good-component lemma to the given $(e,K,G,B,Y,h,L)$. Its hypotheses are precisely the supplied smooth projective semilinear model, all subgroup quotients, and the full-quotient universal-homeomorphism condition on a dense open meeting every component. It gives $F=K^L$, with $[F:e]$ prime to $\ell$ and $K/F$ finite Galois (hence separable), the clopen $Q^\circ\subseteq Y/L$ normal and projective over $F$, its clopen inverse image $Y^\circ$, and the projective surjection $d:Q^\circ\to B$ with every required generic residue degree prime to $\ell$. The restricted finite quotient is $q:Y^\circ\to Q^\circ$. The factorization $h|_{Y^\circ}=dq$ is the restriction of the induced quotient factorization.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, diagram (2.c), p.151; componentwise refinement for the maximal-point residue-degree convention.

proof.text: Put $D^\circ=D\cap Y^\circ$ with its restricted closed subscheme structure. The open-restriction smoothness lemma gives that $Y^\circ$ is smooth over $K$. It is projective over $K$: restrict a closed embedding $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_K$. This restriction is a closed embedding, directly by the closed-immersion definition: its image is closed since $Y^\circ$ is closed in $Y$, and the structure-sheaf map remains surjective, as restriction of sections from $Y$ to its clopen part is projection in the decomposition over the two disjoint opens. Each integral component $D_i$ lies wholly in $Y^\circ$ or wholly in its complement, because $D_i$ is irreducible and these two opens are complementary. Consequently $D^\circ$ consists exactly of the retained $D_i$. Their nonempty intersections are the original intersections, with the same smooth structures and local rings; codimensions are unchanged. The empty intersection is $Y^\circ$, already smooth. The Cartier and reduced conditions restrict locally. Thus $D^\circ$ is a reduced relative strict normal crossings divisor over $K$, by its definition.

source.place: Tag 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize), final assertion; elementary clopen closed-embedding and relative-SNC restriction from the cited definitions; ILO X 2.1 relative-SNC definition, p.149.

proof.text: The set $Y^\circ$ is $L$-stable since it is an inverse image under the invariant quotient, and $D^\circ$ is $L$-stable since $D=(h^{-1}C)_{\rm red}$ and $h$ is invariant. Since every element of $L$ fixes $F=K^L$, the restricted action on $Y^\circ$ is by $F$-scheme automorphisms and remains equivariant over $\operatorname{Spec}K$. By the supplied-quotient geometry lemma applied to $(Y/K,L)$ and the given quotient $Y\to Y/L$, there is a unique $F$-structure on $Y/L$ making the quotient an $F$-morphism; this is the $F$-structure of step 2, and its restriction to the open $Q^\circ$ is the $F$-structure used below. By clopen quotient restriction applied to $Y\to Y/L$ and the open and closed $Q^\circ$, the restriction $q:Y^\circ\to Q^\circ$ is finite surjective, has orbit geometric fibres and invariant structure sheaf, and is categorical; it is an $F$-morphism as the restriction of one. Thus it is the finite categorical geometric quotient required in step 5. Finally $\operatorname{char}F=\operatorname{char}e\neq\ell$; hence the element $\ell^a=|L|$ is nonzero in $F$ and has an inverse. No faithfulness is required.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 3, p.151, tame action over S prime; elementary checks before applying the quotient resolution.

proof.text: Apply the tame semilinear quotient resolution lemma with base field $F$, finite separable extension $K/F$, group $H=L$, scheme $Y^\circ$, invariant divisor $D^\circ$, and quotient $q$. Steps 2--4 check every hypothesis, including invertibility of $|L|$ and projectivity over $K$. Obtain the smooth projective $F$-scheme $R$, the projective surjective $F$-morphism $v:R\to Q^\circ$, and the reduced relative strict normal crossings divisor $E$ with $|E|=v^{-1}(q(|D^\circ|))$. The same lemma gives the bijection on component generic points with equality of residue fields, regularity of $R$, the strict normal crossings boundary assertion, and the local regular-parameter equations. Its nonfaithful-action and empty-divisor clauses apply here.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 3, pp.151--152: componentwise effective tame action, Gabber modification, and logarithmic resolution, assembled by the cited lemma.

proof.text: It remains to identify the boundary support with the inverse image of $C$. If $z\in q(|D^\circ|)$, choose $y\in |D^\circ|$ with $q(y)=z$; then $d(z)=h(y)\in C$. Conversely, if $d(z)\in C$, surjectivity of $q$ gives $y\in Y^\circ$ with $q(y)=z$, and $h(y)=d(z)\in C$, so $y\in |D^\circ|$. Thus $q(|D^\circ|)=d^{-1}(C)$. Taking inverse images under $v$ gives $|E|=(dv)^{-1}(C)$, as required. This also proves the equality when $C$ is empty.
